quotes.text: the most important part of any architecture is documenting your concepts and trying to make it understandable and approachable for the team members.
quotes.speaker: Gabor Ruzsinszki
quotes.why: A clear architectural principle: an architecture only works if the team understands it.

quotes.text: if you are a startup and you are developing an application, then it's an overkill to start with microservices from the beginning because they have a lot of additional effort associated with them.
quotes.speaker: Gabor Ruzsinszki
quotes.why: Concrete, experience-based advice on the monolith-versus-microservices decision.

quotes.text: rest is a market leader because of UIs so the browsers speak natively json and javascript so it's an obvious choice to use rest when you are sending data to an interactive front end.
quotes.speaker: Gabor Ruzsinszki
quotes.why: Explains precisely why gRPC complements rather than replaces REST.

quotes.text: with the rise of AI I would say the most underrated skill at the moment is communication

chapters.title: Meet Gabor Ruzsinszki: from teacher to software architect
Moving to ASP.NET Core and minimal APIs
AI coding assistants, hot takes and career advice

takeaways: WPF remains a solid choice for Windows-only desktop apps, while .NET MAUI or other cross-platform frameworks fit when macOS and other platforms must be supported.
Start with a well-structured monolith and move to microservices only when scale, headcount or explicit requirements justify the extra effort.
gRPC with Protocol Buffers suits fast backend-to-backend communication across languages, while REST stays the natural choice for browser front ends.
hook: .NET developers face a crowded landscape of desktop, web and service technologies, from WPF to ASP.NET Core and gRPC. In this conversation Microsoft MVP Gabor Ruzsinszki helps developers and architects decide when each technology fits, how to approach microservices, and how to use AI assistants without losing core skills.
